subject: Private VPC/on-prem IaC review: Terraform + Helm + CI/CD alignment

Subject: Request: IaC review for private VPC/on-prem rollout

Hi Laura + Redwood team,

Thanks for the demo last week. We're starting the private deployment workstream for Pharma-XYZ and would like Redwood's IaC review and recommendations before we run apply in our staging environment. High-level ask: review our Terraform modules (VPC, transit, on-prem connector), Helm chart changes for the on-prem agent, and the CI/CD pipeline that will orchestrate provisioning and chart deploys.

Attached: terraform plan output (iac-terraform-plan.txt), helm-values.yaml, and a diff of our CI file (gitlab-ci.yml.diff).

Constraints to note:
- Staging is a hybrid: AWS VPC (us-west-2) + on-prem rack in our SF colo.
- On-prem will be air-gapped for production (we plan an internal registry).
- We must prove an auditable run (who applied what) for our compliance team.

Can someone from infra review and send a prioritized list of blockers and quick fixes? Also propose a 30-minute sync—availability this week is: Wed 10–12 PDT or Thu 14–16 PDT.

Thanks,
Samir

Quick checklist we'll cover in the first pass:
- Terraform remote state + lock strategy (S3 + Dynamo / alternative for on-prem)
- KMS/HSM key usage for secrets and state encryption
- CIDR allocation and overlap checks for VPC <> colo networks; transit/peering design
- Bastion/jump host vs proxy pattern for on-prem node access
- Helm values: imagePullSecrets, storage class mapping, node affinity/tolerations for agent pods
- CI gating: plan-only PRs, policy checks (tfsec/checkov), artifact signing for air-gapped registries
- Rollback story and documented runbook for emergency revert

Can you grant read access to the GitHub repo (https://github.com/pharma-xyz/redwood-private-deploy) and add dev_patel@redwood.com? If you prefer, we can also work from the attached diffs.

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, Samir Kapoor <samir.kapoor@pharma-xyz.com>

Subject: Re: Request: IaC review for private VPC/on-prem rollout — initial findings

Samir / Laura — quick first-pass notes after scanning the plan + helm-values: (I'll prepare a short PR checklist and open a repo issue with probes)

Terraform / Networking:
- Module layout: prefer small, idempotent modules (vpc/, transit/, onprem-connector/, dns/) rather than a single monolith. It makes state scoping and rollout safer.
- Remote state: for staged hybrid we recommend S3 backend with server-side encryption (SSE-KMS) and DynamoDB locking. For air-gapped production, use an internal object store with KMS-backed encryption and a locking mechanism (e.g., Consul or Terraform Enterprise remote state). Document how operator creds are rotated.
- CIDR plan: ensure non-overlap; add a validation rule that fails if any customer_cidr overlaps with provided onprem_cidrs. Consider using a /24 per rack mapping and a central allocation module.
- Transit: prefer Transit Gateway in AWS + VLAN-based crossconnect to colo, or BGP session to on-prem router. If TGW is not available, explicit peering + NAT gateways per AZ is OK but harder to scale.
- Bastion vs proxy: for compliance, a bastion with session recording (SSM Session Manager or jump host with auditd/syslog) is better than exposing SSH. Recommend SSM for AWS side and a hardened jump for colo.

Helm / On-prem agent:
- Image registry: since prod will be air-gapped, helm-values should accept an image override and digest pinning (image: repo/agent@sha256:...). Provide an imageMirrors mapping to swap in internal registry addresses.
- Storage: values.yaml must allow per-environment storageClass and persistentVolumeClaim templates for different SAN/NFS backends on colo.
- RBAC & podSecurityContext: ensure non-root user in pods; add a podSecurityPolicy or PSP replacement annotations.

CI/CD / Pipeline:
- Pipeline stages: validate -> plan (tf plan) -> policy scan (tfsec/checkov) -> manual approval -> apply-once-on-controller (with OPA gate). For air-gapped apply, build an artifact bundle that gets physically transferred to the colo runner.
- Secrets: use KMS/HSM + ephemeral runner tokens. Do not bake secrets into images. For GitLab CI, restrict runners to specific tags and require signed commits.
- Gating: require terraform plan in PR comments and restrict merge until plan + policy pass. Save plan binary as artifact so CI can apply the exact plan.

Ansible: only for initial colo provisioning (PXE, disk layout, fuse mount). Keep playbooks idempotent and separate from Terraform state.

Compliance/runbook items:
- Ensure every apply is logged: user, commit SHA, plan artifact, workspace, timestamp. Consider Terraform Cloud/Enterprise or Atlantis with audit hooks if you need richer history.
- Emergency rollback: keep a documented step-by-step (snapshot restore or reverse plan). Test it in staging.

I'll open a PR with a checklist and a few example policies (CIDR overlap check, disallowed open security group) by EOD. For the sync tomorrow, I can present the proposed CI workflow and a short demo of plan audit.

--
Dev Patel
Senior Infrastructure Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Request: IaC review for private VPC/on-prem rollout — constraints and follow-ups

Thanks Dev — this is excellent context. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Production on-prem will be fully air-gapped, so the artifact transfer flow you suggested (bundle -> physical transfer -> colo runner apply) is what we anticipate. We'll likely use an internal Artifactory + signed manifests.
- KMS: we have an HSM-backed KMS on-prem; we expect Redwood to document required KMS operations and least-privilege roles.
- Audit: compliance wants immutable evidence that ties a human operator to the exact apply (commit SHA + plan artifact + runner host). We prefer tooling that stores plan artifacts in an append-only store or sends a copy to an external compliance collector.

Could you include an explicit step-by-step preflight check in the CI that validates: state backend reachable (or alternate preflight for offline), CIDR sanity checks, and image digest presence for helm values. If any of those fail the pipeline should block and create a security ticket.

Also, because of the air-gapped constraint, we'd like an explicit list of required files to be included in the artifact bundle so our operations team can automate packaging.

Appreciate you taking point on the PR/checklist. We can confirm the Thu 3pm PST sync — I accept the invite.

Samir
